chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, which of the people are the most superior in faith?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The most generous of them (those who spread their hand the most).'
ai.seo_question: What characteristic defines the people who are most superior in faith according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) identifies 'abspathuhum kaffan' (those who are most expansive in giving) as the pinnacle of faith, highlighting that true belief manifests through tangible generosity. Shia scholars interpret 'kaff' (hand) metaphorically as the capacity for giving, linking material benevolence directly to spiritual rank. This connects the physical act of charity with the internal state of conviction, a core theme in Twelver Shi'ite ethics.
